answer: A time-locked hash chain makes each identity prove continuous work. On registering, an agent starts a sequential hash chain and must publish the next link each epoch, computable only step by step, never in parallel. At its zenith, one machine can maintain only a few chains, like a river splitting into streams that each need their own bed. A farmer wanting a nebula of fakes must run one chain per identity, paying compute and time for each, while an honest agent runs just one. Forging thousands thus costs thousands of times more than running one, so the attack stops scaling.
